result.title: Exact power indices for plurality-voting ensembles
result.comment: Extended version of a work accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 59 pages, 9 figures, 11 tables
result.summary: Plurality-voting ensembles aggregate the predictions of multiple base classifiers and output the most voted class, with ties typically broken at random. Despite the simple aggregation rule, attributing the impact of each base classifier to the ensemble's predictions is far from straightforward. That is, a single base classifier's impact depends on how it interacts with the votes of all other classifiers in the ensemble, for example, in resolving ties, and not only on its own predictions. We address the attribution problem using established tools from cooperative game theory, studying the Banzhaf and Shapley power indices for new games modeling plurality voting and random tie-breaking, for binary and multiclass classification settings. Computing power indices is, in general, intractable. Surprisingly, our methods, collectively named ENPOWER, enable the exact computation of Banzhaf and Shapley values in linear time for the binary classification setting and in low-degree polynomial time for the multiclass setting. The algorithms in ENPOWER rely on new combinatorial formulations of the Banzhaf and Shapley indices, yielding closed-form solutions for the binary case and ordinary generating function representations for the multiclass case. We validate empirically the methods in ENPOWER demonstrating their high applicability, providing attribution values not captured by existing methods. We apply the attribution of ENPOWER to: ensemble pruning and prompt-based ensembling of vision-language models.

AI.brief_summary: 论文用合作博弈论为多数投票集成（含随机打破平局）构造新博弈，研究 Banzhaf 与 Shapley 权力指数，提出 ENPOWER 使二分类可线性时间、多分类可低次多项式时间精确计算，并用于集成裁剪与 VLM 的 prompt 集成。
AI.relevance_reason: 其 Shapley/Banzhaf 的精确、可扩展计算线索，可能可供核查 LVR 中多组件或推理步骤的贡献分配与诊断问题，但原论文归因对象是分类器投票而非内部推理状态，迁移性需自行验证。
